candidates.name: Basra–Haditha–Ceyhan Oil Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Basra Oil Company / Chevron (US) / Capital TI (US) / UCC Holding (Qatar); Basra-Haditha section studies by KBR
candidates.from: Rumaila/Basra oil fields (via Haditha, Kirkuk, Fishkhabur, Silopi)

evidence.note: Iraq cabinet (5 Jul 2026) approved non-binding heads-of-agreement with Chevron/Capital TI (US)/UCC (Qatar) consortium for feasibility studies comparing a Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan route vs a Basra-Haditha-Baniyas route; preliminary/exploratory only.

Iraqi oil minister Basim Khudair describes 'a crude pipeline system linking Basra with Faysh Khabur and Turkey's Mediterranean port of Ceyhan'; ~2 million bpd capacity per unnamed officials; unclear whether route crosses KRG territory.
US-based Capital TI/Chevron and Qatar's UCC consortium named to build pipeline network from Basra to Fishkhabur, extending onward to Ceyhan (Turkey) or Baniyas (Syria) as alternative outlets.
Confirms Qatar-US consortium set to sign deal for Iraq oil pipeline studies, corroborating the Basra-northward routing to the Turkish/Syrian Mediterranean coast.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Distinct from any single roster PID: the southern leg overlaps P0544 (Basra->Haditha, construction) and the eventual Turkish leg overlaps P0547 (Kirkuk->Ceyhan, operating), but the connecting segment carrying this project's identity — Haditha north through Kirkuk/Fishkhabur/Silopi to Ceyhan — has no matching PID (P1854, the closest, is a cancelled Beji–Fishkhabur replacement at only 350km/1,000,000bpd, not framed as a Basra-sourced through-line). Sponsor set (Chevron/Capital TI/UCC) and July 2026 cabinet approval are new information not reflected in any existing roster row.

candidates.name: Basra–Haditha–Baniyas Oil Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Basra Oil Company / Chevron (US) / Capital TI (US) / UCC Holding (Qatar)

evidence.note: Names 'Basra-Haditha-Baniyas route, targeting the Syrian Mediterranean coast' as one of two alternative routes under the same July 2026 feasibility-study agreement.
Oil minister describes 'a branch from Haditha to Syria's Baniyas' as part of the same pipeline-system studies, alongside the Ceyhan option.
Describes the pipeline network as extending to 'the Syrian port of Baniyas' as an alternative outlet to Ceyhan.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Overlaps in destination with the existing Kirkuk–Baniyas Oil Pipelines family (P0546/P5277/P5278/P5279/P7913), but this 2026 proposal explicitly originates at Basra/Rumaila and routes via Haditha, not from Kirkuk — a materially different southern origin and alignment under a new Chevron/Capital TI/UCC-led feasibility study, distinct from the separately-reviving historic Kirkuk-Baniyas line (which Iraq and Syria are pursuing on its own track per Aug-Nov 2025 talks).
